scams.name: Ao Nang Taxi & Tuk-Tuk Mafia Overcharge + Grab Blocking
scams.description: You want to get from Ao Nang beach to Tiger Cave Temple, 25 km away. You open Grab and book — 280 baht in the app. The driver messages you: ‘Cannot pick up Ao Nang, sorry, taxi mafia.’ You walk one block inland; same message. You give up and flag a *tuk-tuk* on the main Ao Nang strip. The driver quotes 1,500 baht each way, 2,500 round trip, no meter, no negotiation. r/ThailandTourism ‘Was I scammed? Ao Nang taxi mafia’ confirms: ‘The taxi mafia exists. In some places in town, Grab drivers won’t even pick you up — they refuse the drive.’ The Ao Nang taxi cartel is one of the most aggressive in Thailand, physically intimidating Grab drivers who enter their zone and holding a fixed inflated price list.
scams.avoidance: Walk 500 meters inland from the Ao Nang beach strip to the main road before you request a Grab. This is the community-verified workaround. Know the benchmark Grab fares: Ao Nang to Krabi Town 200 baht, Ao Nang to Tiger Cave 280, Ao Nang to KBV airport 350. At Krabi airport (KBV), use the metered taxi counter inside arrivals — not drivers outside the terminal. Grab works normally from Krabi Town bus terminal (not Ao Nang); take the 150-baht shuttle bus from Ao Nang to the bus terminal and Grab from there. Photograph the tuk-tuk plate if overcharged and report to Tourist Police on 1155; Krabi has documented mafia complaints and occasional enforcement.
scams.location: Ao Nang main beach strip, Klong Muang Road, Krabi Town bus terminal, Krabi airport

scams.name: Scooter Rental Passport-Hostage Damage
scams.description: You rent a scooter on Ao Nang’s main strip for 250 baht a day. The shop asks for your passport as deposit — every shop on the block does. You ride for five days without incident. On return, the owner’s wife points to a scratch on the underside of the fairing — barely visible, almost certainly pre-existing — and demands 12,000 baht. Your passport is in their safe. Your flight is tomorrow. r/Thailand ‘I rented motorbike from scam company in Krabi. Help’ documents the pattern specifically for Ao Nang. The Krabi variant uses the same passport-hostage leverage as Phuket and Chiang Mai, with damage quotes typically running five to fifteen times the real repair cost.
scams.avoidance: Never hand over your original passport. Offer a 3,000–5,000 baht cash deposit and a photocopy of the identification page; walk from any shop that refuses. Smile Bike Ao Nang and Krabi Motorbike Center both accept cash deposits. Before driving off, photograph every panel of the scooter (including the underside) timestamped, and email copies to yourself. Point out every existing scratch to the owner out loud on video before you leave. If a damage claim is made on return, get an independent repair quote at a Honda or Yamaha dealership in Krabi Town before paying. Call Krabi Tourist Police on 1155 or visit the Ao Nang beach police box if the shop won’t return your passport — response time is typically under 30 minutes.
scams.location: Ao Nang main road rental shops, Krabi Town, Railay backpacker rentals

scams.name: 4-Island Longtail Boat Tour Overcharge
scams.description: You walk up to a longtail-boat pier at Ao Nang and ask for a 4-Island tour (Chicken Island, Poda, Tup, and Pranang/Railay). The booth quotes 3,500 baht per person. You take it. At the next hotel’s tour desk, the going rate is 800–1,200 baht per person for the same trip — less than a third. r/ThailandTourism ‘Just got back from Krabi, here’s what you need to know’ confirms: ‘Half day, pretty cheap — around 800–1,200 baht — and hits all the Instagram spots.’ r/ThailandTourism ‘Recommendations for krabi 4 Island tour’ gives the community consensus: roughly 500 baht variance depending on which pier you leave from. The overcharge is a 2× to 5× markup for walking up to the wrong booking booth.
scams.avoidance: Book 4-Island, Hong Islands, or Phi Phi tours on 12go.asia or Klook — verified operators, fixed prices, digital receipts. If booking at the pier, compare three to five booths before accepting any quote; 50–100 percent variance is normal. Know the benchmarks: 4-Island shared 800–1,200 baht per person, Hong Islands 1,200–1,800 per person, private longtail (up to four people) 2,200–3,500 baht total. Pay by credit card when possible — chargebacks resolve fly-by-night operator issues. For Phi Phi, use Sea Star Andaman, Songserm, or the Chao Koh ferry; all have official websites with fixed pricing.
scams.location: Ao Nang beach pier, Klong Muang pier, Krabi Town Chao Fah pier, Ao Nam Mao pier

scams.name: Tiger Cave Temple Transport & Entry Manipulation
scams.description: You finally find a Grab driver willing to make the Ao Nang to Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Sua) round trip for 700 baht. At the temple entrance, a ‘tourist assistant’ in an unofficial uniform approaches and says the summit (1,237 steps) requires a 300-baht-per-person access fee, and offers a guided walk for 1,500. Tiger Cave Temple is free to enter. The summit climb is free. There is no access fee. r/ThailandTourism ‘What could have happened here?’ flags Tiger Cave directly: ‘It’s a well-known scam place. Check their Google reviews — lots of one-star stories about being overcharged.’
scams.avoidance: Enter Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Sua) expecting to pay nothing — it is genuinely free. Use Grab round-trip, or pre-book an honest taxi via your hotel for 700–1,000 baht; don’t use Route 4 turnoff tuk-tuks. Bring your own water and snacks — the 1,237-step climb has no food or water stations, and entrance vendors overcharge. Ignore anyone offering a ‘guide’ — the path is simply stairs up and stairs down, with no decision points. If harassed by an ‘official,’ walk past them toward the monastery; the temple staff will disperse the scammers.
scams.location: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Sua), 25 km from Ao Nang, access road tuk-tuk stands

scams.name: Phi Phi / Maya Bay Ferry Ticket & National Park Fee Double-Billing
scams.description: You book a Koh Phi Phi speedboat day tour at an Ao Nang booth for 1,800 baht. At the boat, the operator demands an additional 400 baht ‘national park entrance fee’ for Maya Bay. You pay. On the boat, another tourist tells you his tour already included the park fee in the 1,800 — you paid twice. The Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Koh Phi Phi National Park entry fee is 400 baht for foreigners (40 baht for Thais, the legally sanctioned 10× foreigner price) and must be paid, but it is often bundled into tour prices. Scam booths exclude it from their quote and extract it a second time at the boat. r/ThailandTourism ‘So what’s the deal with the Maya Bay entrance’ documents the ambiguity.
scams.avoidance: Book Phi Phi ferries directly with Chao Koh Ferry or Songserm on their official sites — 300–450 baht one-way. Book Phi Phi day tours on 12go.asia or Klook with ‘park fee included’ explicit in the listing; confirm in writing before paying. Bring 400 baht per person in cash for the national park fee regardless; if the tour says included, you have a backup. Keep the printed Klook or 12go voucher on you on the boat; operators occasionally try to double-bill even on prepaid tours. If overcharged, get a receipt for everything, file with Tourist Police on 1155 within 24 hours, and dispute the credit card charge.
scams.location: Krabi Town Klong Chilad pier, Ao Nang beach pier, tourist booking booths island-wide

scams.name: Ao Nang Hair Supplement / Weight Loss Street Pitch
scams.description: Walking on Ao Nang’s main strip in the late afternoon, a well-dressed man approaches, compliments your appearance, mentions he is a visiting doctor from Dubai, and shows you before-and-after photos of men with restored hair or women with dramatic weight loss. He offers a small bottle of ‘Ayurvedic oil’ or a ‘certified weight-loss supplement’ at 3,000 baht, ‘special price, only today.’ r/ThailandTourism ‘Potential Turkish/Indian scam at Ao Nang’ documents it directly: ‘It’s really a scam if someone says belly fat will be lost without any change in food or exercise, especially in 21 days.’ The same crew rotates between Pattaya, Phuket, and Ao Nang — same scripts, same props.
scams.avoidance: Don’t engage. Reply ‘no thanks’ and keep walking — the conversation is the setup. Buy supplements only at Boots, Watsons, or Tesco Lotus in Krabi Town with posted fixed prices. Never follow a stranger to a ‘consultation’ room; real medical advice is at a clinic, not a storefront. If you are already inside, pay by credit card in baht, save the receipt, and file a chargeback immediately. Report rotating crews to Krabi Tourist Police on 1155 — they have made arrests on this category in 2024–2025.
scams.location: Ao Nang main beach strip (Soi Ao Nang 4–12), Krabi Town night market

scams.name: Ao Nang Bar Lady Drinks & Pad Thai Tourist Pricing
scams.description: You’re at a Reggae Bar or open-front bar on Ao Nang’s Soi 12 and a hostess sits down. She orders a 150-baht drink and you pay for her one. Thirty minutes and three of her drinks later, the bill is 2,500 baht and you’ve paid for companionship you didn’t quite agree to. The scam is a milder, beach-variant of Pattaya’s bar-girl escalation — lower dollar amounts, same mechanic. r/ThailandTourism ‘Is Railay beach expensive???’ documents the broader pattern: ‘Ao Nang is also scamfest central, where many places charge 200+ baht for pad Thai’ — a dish that costs 60–80 baht in Krabi Town.
scams.avoidance: At bars, choose venues with a posted menu and no street recruiters; pay each drink individually. For restaurants, walk two or three blocks inland from the main Ao Nang strip — prices drop 40 to 60 percent. Benchmark Ao Nang prices: pad Thai 60–80 baht local, 150–250 tourist strip; Chang beer 70 baht local, 150 tourist; smoothie 40 baht local, 100 tourist. Filter Google Maps for restaurants with 100+ reviews and a 4.3+ average; tourist-pricing traps usually carry lower ratings. At the Ao Nang night market and Krabi Town night market, prices run close to local — use these for most meals.
scams.location: Ao Nang Center Point bar area, Soi 12, Reggae Bar strip, beachfront restaurants
